exposure: more than one previously vaginal delivery
cesarean section during the first stage of labor
Mode of delivery (prelabor cesarean, cesarean during labor, first vaginal delivery, multiple vaginal deliveries)
outcome: Perineal body dimensions (length, height, perimeter, area)
finding: Pregnancy and delivery, regardless of mode, resulted in significant decreases in perineal body length, perimeter, and area measured at 6 weeks postpartum.
mod_finding: While cesarean section was associated with smaller changes in perineal body dimensions compared to vaginal delivery, it did not completely prevent these changes.
